key_insight: A validated lattice-Boltzmann data pipeline is being used to create reproducible 3D turbulent channel-flow benchmarks for testing neural-operator surrogates.
engineering_relevance: This provides a standardized, physics-checked dataset and benchmark workflow for comparing CFD surrogates on forecasting, super-resolution, and error-correction tasks in turbulent flows.
method: Generate 3D obstructed channel-flow cases with controlled geometries at Re = 1,000–10,000.
Run a cumulant-collision LBM solver and validate it against experimental Strouhal number, drag, and turbulence statistics.
Use the dataset to evaluate Fourier Neural Operators and U-Net variants with physics-informed metrics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comprehensive grid-convergence studies at 1024×512×512 and validation against experimental measurements of Strouhal number, drag coefficients, and turbulent fluctuations.
watch_item: The planned surrogate benchmarks still depend on how well the chosen metrics capture turbulent energy-cascade fidelity and fair comparison across model types.
paper_title: A Validated LBM Dataset and Pipeline for Surrogate Modeling of Turbulent 3D Obstructed Channel Flows
